utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. I hope there is a translation. Is there any translation? Yes. Well, first of all, we deeply regret the delay which is caused by the absence of the -- strange absence of the technicians. We have decided anyway to start, although we are only getting a transcript later on, there will be no live notes for the time being, but we hope that by the time we move on to substantial matters we may have the technicians available. Now, first of all, let me deal with two preliminary issues, housekeeping matters. We have received a motion from the Defence relating to the calling by the Court of a Judge, the Judge -- I don't know whether I can say her name, and the other witness, the lady whose name cannot be disclosed. Now, I understand before we serve those summonses, the relevant authorities would like to know the date when those witnesses should be called here. Since we are calling those witnesses at the request of Defence counsel, we were wondering whether the Defence counsel could suggest a date so that we can put a date in the relevant documents to be sent over to the competent authorities. I wonder whether you could quickly consult with one another and decide what to do. Yes, please, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. President. We would like if these two witnesses could come together so that we could hear them together, and we suggest that it takes place sometime in April because this witness will be questioned by several Defence counsel. So we propose that this takes place sometime in April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. This means that this should be between the 26th and the 29th of April. We have only four working days available, I'm afraid, because as you know, the 30th is Queen's Day, it's a holiday. I wonder -- thank you. Any comments from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good. So we can move on to other matters. As you have realised, as you know, the -- one of the Judges, Judge May, is ill and is not likely to attend our hearings before Monday, because he has been taken ill with a serious flu. We were wondering whether the other party pursuant to Rule 71 was prepared to put in a request that we should take their positions so that we can go on and not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Indeed, sir. Your Honour, the Prosecution is prepared to make that formal request of the Chamber, that you can sit as presiding officers under Rule 71(A), and hear depositions in the remaining days of this week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: What about Defence counsel? In particular I would like to ask Counsel Puliselic whether he would also agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Yesterday we were informed that Judge May was ill, and we immediately made contact with the detention unit and requested to see the accused Dragan Papic, and I have to inform you that the accused Dragan Papic is opposed to the witnesses being questioned before only two Judges of the Chamber. These are very important witnesses for him. These are fact witnesses, and they will be speaking about incidents he had has been charged with in the relevant times. So it is the proposal of the Defence that these witnesses be not heard before two Judges of the Chamber only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Puliselic, but before we make a ruling on this matter I would like to explain to you how we see these proceedings covered by Rule 71 depositions. When the trial is underway, in practice what happens is that the Judge who is absent because of serious impediments, after the taking of the deposition by two officers, will go through the transcript and normally he can watch a videotape with the testimony given by the witness and will also watch the examination-in-chief, cross-examination and so on. So in a way, we don't see any huge difference between the resort to this particular procedure, their positions, and actual trial proceedings. There's no -- on the practical side -- legally speaking, of course, there is a difference. On the practical speaking there is no difference whatsoever, because the Judge, by simply reading carefully the transcript of all our proceedings, plus watching the videotape, can make his own conviction and can decide on the credibility of a witness. In light of that, do you still insist on your opposition to the application of Rule 71? I may add, before that, this also happened to me last week. Remember, I was ill and only one witness was heard under Rule 71, and I proceeded in that manner. I can now form my own conviction about the credibility of that witness by simply working afterwards at home or here in office hours, in the afternoon. So could you please let us know whether you insist on your opposition?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, when you were ill the situation was different. We agreed that witnesses be heard, witnesses relating to general allegations, but these witnesses will be speaking about some very specific circumstances, and I'm simply conveying to you what the accused Dragan Papic told me. He told his Defence counsel that he did not wish witnesses to be heard before two Judges of the Chamber only, and we hope that the illness of Judge May is not serious and we do expect that he will soon be available and here. So we would suggest that these witnesses not be heard until that time, until the Chamber is able to sit in full composition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We rule that in spite of the opposition of the Defence counsel and the accused, Rule 71 is fully applicable because according to this Rule the request of one party is sufficient, and we feel that we are confronted with exceptional circumstances and that the interests of justice command that a fair and expeditious trial be held. As I said before, since in any case the Judge who is presently absent will be able fully to form his own conviction, legal conviction and opinion, I think there will be nothing which would jeopardise the rights of the accused. So we decide to proceed accordingly, and I would be acting as a presiding officer, and we will, therefore, under Rule 71(E), subsequently transmit the record to the Trial Chamber in its full composition so that Judge May will be in a position to appraise the evidence and be fully familiar with it. It is decided accordingly, and we may now move on to the first witness to be examined-in-chief by counsel Nika Pinter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder if any protective measures have been requested?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Papic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pinter?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Papic. Would you please introduce yourself to the Judges? You may remain seated.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: My name is Pero Papic. I was born on the 15th of June, 1965 in the village of Santici in Vitez, the municipality of Vitez, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: On the aerial photograph of Ahmici, could you please point to your house?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: May I stand up?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, you may, and you may take the pointer.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: This is my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you state other houses that are in your village, and could you please speak slowly?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: This is the house of my mother Marija Papic, the house of Nakic, Mehmed Ahmic, the house of Ivo Papic, the house of Nikica Milicevic, the house of Rafael Milicevic, Alija Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Have you indicated all the houses?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You may sit down. Mr. Papic, in the area around your house was there a shelter, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a shelter in the basement of my house, which was approximately 20 square metres large.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When was it used as a shelter?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It was used sometime in mid 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did all of your neighbours come to your shelter? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The neighbours who lived in the immediate vicinity used to come to our shelter but also people who lived in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I will now ask several questions, but would you please wait a little before you give your answer? In the vicinity of your house, was there a forest?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who are the owners of the forest?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The owners of the forest are Anto Papic, Simo Vidovic, Gavro Vidovic, Marko Papic and Ivo Papic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How is Ivo Papic related to you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Ivo Papic is my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Which means that Dragan Papic is your cousin?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us a little bit what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We had organised ourselves, the residents of the houses that lived in the vicinity of my house. We organised the village guards on our own.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were there only Croats who participated in the village guards or were there any Muslims maybe?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: There were also Muslims as of mid 1992 approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was there any sort of command over the village guards?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. As I told you, we had organised ourselves on our own.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were. We were given some old rifles, M-48 rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who gave them to you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the village guards in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The Croats did not have a commander of the village guards, and I don't know about Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you stand guard with Muslims all the time or did at one -- did you separate at one point?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Until the night of the 19th of October, 1992 we stood village guards together with Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us the events that took place on the 19th and the 20th, but slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of October, 1992, Fahran Ahmic came to see us that night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Where were you that night?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: That night I was on duty as part of our regular village guard. Vidovic Vinko was with me, Ivica Papic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who is Papic Ivica?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Ivica Papic is my late brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And where were you, please?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I was at my own home, in the vicinity of my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: While you were on guard, Fahrudin came?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Just before nightfall, Fahran came, and we asked him, as we kept guard duty together, we asked him why they wouldn't join us that night. He didn't give us any answer; he simply turned around and went off home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else while you were on guard duty?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, we simply felt some changes in the air. This was the greatest change, because that night, Fahran withdrew from our common guards, and Salim Causevic said, "Am I going to stay with you, or should I keep guard duty on my own?" We asked what he meant, and we simply didn't understand, nor did we realise that the situation was serious.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: While you were on guard duty, did you see some people moving around the fence?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did notice that, and that is why we asked Fahran, but he gave us no answer. As far as we knew, the most probable explanation was that he warned them, and then we didn't see them again during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you warn anyone about seeing those people?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We didn't need to in our immediate vicinity. We didn't think it was necessary, so we didn't warn anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And then what happened during the night and in the morning?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We kept duty as usual. I was on duty. With me were Rafael Milicevic, Ivica Papic, Vinko Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And before dawn, what happened?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Just before it dawned, about 4.45 a.m., I can't tell you exactly what time it was, but roughly it was about that time, very heavy gunfire was opened at my house, coming from the fence which was about 20 metres away from my house, to the west of my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: This burst of fire came from several weapons. There were some explosive devices which we could not identify, most probably handmade devices. Then some ten minutes later, the firing subsided. This was about 5.00. When we heard the call from the minaret of the mosque, first there was some music. We couldn't explain it, we couldn't recognise it. Then there was a speech, somebody saying "Croats, surrender." Then in the central part of the village, an explosion could be heard. After that, I sought to save my family and my houses. I had -- my wife and my child were in the house, and my brother-in-law's -- my wife's brother's child, who was between 6 and 7 at the time. When the shooting subsided I ran into the house, because the entrance to the house is on the northern side. There are steps on both sides. I ran in from the west, because of course I was afraid of further shooting. I entered the house and the room that faces south-east. This was my good fortune that it was positioned in that way, because later on, we realised that my wife was packing things into a sleeping bag, children's things of my little girl.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you manage to see the damage done to your house?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: When my wife asked me to get some things from the living room, I wasn't aware of what had happened. I just saw that the door was broken in. But I never realised the chaos that the living room would be in. Even the dust hadn't settled, nor the smoke that was still evident in the rooms. I was surprised; dust was still floating around. I trod on broken glass. I entered; I picked up the things as quickly as I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What about the children?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: When I passed these things on to my wife, then we threw out a pillow first, through the western side of the house, through the window. It isn't very high; it is about 2 metres high. So we threw out a pillow to help them land, to soften their fall.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When you dropped the children down, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Then I went towards the main door, and there was a thick fog, so visibility was very limited. It was about 10 to 15 metres. I went out, and I told my wife that she should run out too. I pushed her through the back door, and then together with them, because we were scared, we passed by my mother's house towards the nearby wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that later on, but let me ask you first: Apart in your house, on the 20th of October, which other houses were damaged, and were other houses damaged?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The house of Mehmed Ahmic, known as Sudjuka, his house was damaged; Drago Josipovic's house, and the barn had burnt down. And another barn near my house, owned by Alija Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Of course you are talking about the part of the village where you lived, not about the whole area?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I didn't know what had happened elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Tell us now, you mentioned Alija Ahmic's barn that was on fire; who put the fire out on that barn?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We did. Me, my brother; Vinko helped us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And where was Alija?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: They had left early in the morning. His daughter and mother had left before that. We didn't know that. They had left before, earlier on. And immediately after the gunfire started, they probably saw that they hadn't done what they were meant to do, and they left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So the house was deserted and the barn was burning?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We didn't manage to extinguish the fire in the barn but only in part of the house that had caught fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When you took the children out of the house, you and your wife, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: All of us who were there, we consulted as to what we should do next. We had sought refuge in the small wood. We felt safe there, but we didn't know what to do next. So we realised that the only direction we could take would be southwards, towards Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And who went with you? Who did you lead?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: At the time, Ankica managed to join us; my mother, too, they live across the road, and her children.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We went towards the wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you show us with the pointer where this is?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You may get up.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: So we went across the centre of the wood. We formed a group there. We gathered, and then we headed towards -- in this direction. Dragan Papic went in front of us with his wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you follow them?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We knew who was in front and who was behind us. And we could tell mostly by the voices. Here, somebody just said "Stop, or I'll shoot." Those of us behind, we just dropped to the ground. We were scared, of course, and Dragan remained in front of me, and we just heard a conversation. Some words were exchanged; of course we couldn't decipher what was being said. But roughly it was that nobody would hurt us and that we could go on. Nenad Santic was there. Nenad Santic. Dragan went ahead. He crossed the embankment where the old railway line was. I sent my wife and children, as I have already said. I just told them to go on, without saying anything as to where and when. I just said that they should cross the river, over the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: If the visibility was so poor, how did you know it was Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: By his voice, because we are close neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you see him coming?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the time was, roughly?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: About 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know where Dragan Papic went from there? Did you see him after that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: He went to Rovna. I didn't see him again that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you recollect, when was the road opened to traffic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. I can't tell you exactly. Maybe plus or minus one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, did you know why the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, I had no idea why fire was opened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When did you learn the reason?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What did you learn?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of October, I learned the details and the purpose of that conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And what was the cause that provoked the conflict? What happened near the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I learned subsequently that a roadblock had been put up that night we didn't know about it. A roadblock had been set up for the Croatian army, the HVO that was supposed to pass along the Busovaca/Vitez road in the direction of Jajce to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you go -- of course not on that day, but later on -- to see what things looked like where the roadblock was put up?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did, because we were curious to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We saw trenches which had been dug across the road from the cemetery, and in the cemetery itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You could see them dug out?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You said that you learnt the next day the reason. Who did you talk to, and how did you learn the causes and the reasons of that conflict? Could you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The next day, on the 21st of October, Muris Ahmic came along the road. We were just below my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When you say "we," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Vinko, my brother Zoran at the time, Ivica Papic, Rafael Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you were standing?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were standing there, and he asked whether he could approach us. We said, "why not? Do, come up, and let's see what this is all about." He came up close to us. He had some big boots on him. He was rather dirty. He approached us and he started crying. We asked him why he was crying. "Why did you do this to us?" He said that he headed the operation. He told us the details of the operation, what the aim of the operation was. He told us as follows; "The aim of the operation, which I was told to lead, I was given orders from the command, from Muharem Sivro, the task, because he was meant to be the leader but he passed it on to me. We were supposed to chase out the Croats. We had permission to take whatever we liked from the houses and then to set them on fire so that the Croats could not come back. This was the closest way for us to link up with others, to intercept communication, to link up with Gornja Rovna and Vranjska."

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And Muris Ahmic told you all this?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was his statement. Then he started apologising, what could we do, could we go back. "We know nothing about that, whether you can come back or not, but we can't tell you that you can't either. It's up to you to decide." Afterwards I learned that there was a meeting between the Croats and the Muslim leaders. This is from hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, but you yourself did not have any direct contact?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In this conversation with Muris Ahmic, was there any mention about the positions of the BH army units? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, but we assumed. We knew roughly where they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How did you know, and where were they as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We knew because the people who came that day, we asked him where those men had come from, and they were from Vrhovine and they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So he told you that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. That they were from Vrhovine, and some were from Poculica and Preocica. He didn't go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were they wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Tell us, in the actual fighting over the roadblock near the cemetery, did the Croats from Ahmici take part?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: They couldn't participate because we didn't know anything about it, so we couldn't take part. In fact, we were shot at.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In your mother's house or in your house was any kind of material kept, boxes of ammunition or anything like that? Was there any kind of -- were any kind of weapons stored in your house or your mother's house?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know Fahrudin Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He's my very close neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What were relations like?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We were good neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. We assisted one another. He had just started to build his house. Actually, at the time it had already been completed, but we helped him build it. His immediate next door neighbour, Alija Ahmic, would not let him connect to the electricity supply in his house, so we allowed him to do it, to connect to my mother's house. Then also he connected to the water supply system to our house, though it wasn't intended for use by more users, but we allowed him to use it. And we exchanged visits. He would visit us, we would visit them. This was quite customary amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Tell us, on the 20th of October did all the Muslims leave Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I couldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: But could you tell us about your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. We do know that all of them left, the people on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When did they come back?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: They started coming back when the Croats called them to come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was this a month or two later?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, no, two days later. Around the 22nd already they started coming back en masse.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did anyone enter the Muslim homes when they abandoned them? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, not one -- none of us went into those houses, because that was the way we were brought up, that in such a situation we shouldn't take advantage of such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So they were not looted?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the second conflict that occurred between the Muslims and the Croats in Ahmici, any personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge, only what I heard later on from others.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In April 1993, were you in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Where was your family?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In April 1993.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: In April you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I had a car accident on the 10th of February, 1993, so that my family was with me in Busovaca when I was released from hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you were nowhere near Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So on the 15th of April you didn't come to pick up your wife in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because she was with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Before you had that car accident you lived in Ahmici, until February 1993, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In that period did you socialise with Dragan?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you have frequent contacts?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can't remember exactly how often we met but frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was his appearance the same as it is now?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. He had a much bigger beard.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What were the comments regarding his beard?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We all said that he should shave it off because of the situation, the attacks by the army and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So he wore a bigger beard than he has now?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: If you recall, where was Dragan working? What was his job?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan was working in the Sumarija, the forestry company of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How did he go to work? Was he wearing civilian clothes or a uniform? What kind of uniform did he have? How was he dressed usually?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: As for the details of his dress, I'm not an expert. It's very hard for me to say that, because this is not something that I notice very much on people, but I know that he used to wear a uniform from time to time. He did not participate in the village guards so much because he was engaged elsewhere. He couldn't be in two places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did he carry a rifle?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes he carried a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What was he doing in his spare time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: In his spare time Dragan repaired cars, and he was also very good at repairing electrical devices in cars, which was not very ordinary because he was not an expert for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did he distinguish amongst people whose cars he repaired?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. He repaired cars of everyone, Croats and Muslims alike.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Since you socialised with him, did you ever hear any nationalistic comments from him? Was he only in favour of the Croatian cause? Was he against Serbs and Muslims, other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. He never expressed himself in that way because he's a very good man.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was he any kind of political -- was he politically involved in Ahmici in any way?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. He didn't like politics very much. He only likes cars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: While you lived in Ahmici until February 1993, throughout that period did Dragan train Croatian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Train Croatian soldiers? No. How could Dragan possibly do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was he in charge of any political gatherings or political meetings?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. This was not something that he was interested in.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The family of Dragan Papic, the family of your uncle, was there any member from that family who showed any signs of nationalistic orientation, who made any differences amongst people on the basis their nationality?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. We never felt that in any way in the entire family of ours, I mean, all of us. We didn't make any differences. We didn't notice anything in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How much do you know about the mosque and the way it was built?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I know quite a few things about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you -- could you describe that for us a little bit? And I'm referring to the lower mosque.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know who the contractor was? Did your neighbours help build the mosque?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. There was this man whom we called Hadzija. He was the main donor for that purpose, and he was in charge of building the mosque. We all gave something at the very beginning when the foundations were being laid. We all made our contribution. It's a custom in our village and everybody did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you also work there?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the mosque was finished, when the construction of the mosque was finished, my uncle did some plumbing work and I also helped, myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you charge them for that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, it was not normally charged. We never charged our services for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So your uncle didn't ask for any payment?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. No. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Dragan helping his father during his free time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever he had free time he would help his father. When there was a lot of work to do he tried to help him as much as he could.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What were your activities in 1992-1993, before your accident?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I'm an electrical engineer, and I also worked in the field of electronics. I repaired TV sets, radio sets and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you repair appliances of all people in your village?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would go to Muslim houses, Croat houses alike. This was my job ever since 1984.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you know Mehmed Ahmic Sudzuka well?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: He was your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In your neighbourhood did Sudzuka have a close relative of his?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had some close family there, Alija's sons, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What are their names?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Abdulah Ahmic, Munir Ahmic, Muris Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. That means that Abdulah Ahmic and Mehmed Ahmic are related in the same way as you and Dragan are related?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What was Mehmed Ahmic doing? What was his job?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: He was involved in politics, and he had a shop in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he belonged to any political party?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What did you think of him, and do you know what other people thought of him and what were your relations with him?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew what people thought about him. People didn't really like him, Croats and Muslims alike, because he had debts to many people, something having to do with the construction of his new house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the distance is between your house and the house of Mehmed Ahmic? You don't need to be very precise.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: You mean between my house?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, between your husband and the house of Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And what would be the distance between the house of Mehmed Ahmic and the wood we discussed earlier on?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: About 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can I ask the assistance of the usher, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D26/5.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the land registry of the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who normally issues such documents?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Such a document would normally be issued by land registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you see the entire house of yours on this document?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The whole house is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What about the wood?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The wood is not here, not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can I again have the assistance of the usher, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D27/5.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Have you had a look at it? This is something that -- it's called the area situation. Can you see this document? On this document you can see the distances between facilities. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you think that that realistically depicts a situation on the ground? Do these distances correspond to the distances between Mehmed Ahmic's house, the edge of the wood and so on?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't think that everything is here. This portion, for example, this portion of the wood is missing from the plan, so the distance is even greater now. Well, I don't know about the period then.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, but the distance between the house and the edge of the wood from the left side or from the right side?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is okay. It was next to the edge of the wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move back to the month of October 1992, the 20th of October, to be more precise. On that day, from the wood behind your house, from any part of the wood, did anyone shoot at the house of Mehmed Ahmic from any kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: To the best my knowledge nobody shot from that area, because I spent most of that day in the middle of the wood because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: On that day and on subsequent days, near the house of your mother and near the house of Ivo Papic, in the direction of the house of Ljubica Milicevic, was there ever a PAT or a PAM weapon that was sited there?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, it was never there. It was impossible to site that weapon in that area because of the number of small children in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's microphone be switched on, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you are sure that on the 20th of October, nobody opened fire from the wood on the house of Sudjuka?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. From our wood, nobody opened fire on the house of Sudjuka.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was Dragan with you in the wood?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. Dragan was absent throughout that day, the 20th of October, and later on I heard he had spent the whole day in Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about weapons in general?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise most types.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The PAT and the PAM, what kind of weapons are they, the anti-aircraft weapons? Are they long-range weapons?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: We have seen that the distance was 150 metres, approximately. Is that a long distance for that type of weapon? Is it efficient on that distance?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: One cannot adequately position that kind of weapon this kind of distance. This is simply too close for it, and it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The house of Mehmed Ahmic you said was damaged, at the beginning, it was damaged during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, what caused the damage on the house? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, at one point we realised that the house was damaged, that the roof of the house was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What caused the damage of the roof?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It was caused by some kind of impact.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, we couldn't see that. We simply heard that. And after that the house caught fire, and because of the way it was built, because of the construction of the house and the number of beams and lumber, it caught fire very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: This is what you learned later on?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So according to your opinion, the house was probably hit in the roof area?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dragan carry or fire from a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think that he ever owned a sniper rifle, and I never saw him with one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you see him or did you hear any complaints about his intimidating Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: In view of his character, I don't think that Dragan would ever intimidate anyone or verbally abuse anyone, and I never heard any stories like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who lived in the house of Ivo Papic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Ivo Papic; Dragica Papic; Ivanka Papic, Dragan's sister; Goran Papic; and Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know when Dragan's wife gave birth to Marin?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I know that it happened in late April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When did you see Dragan in that time, for the first time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It was in mid-1993, or even later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Let us go back to your neighbours. You said that Abdulah Ahmic and Mehmed Ahmic were cousins?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What about Muris Ahmic? Is he in any way related to Abdulah Ahmic and Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Muris is Abdulah's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes my examination of this witness, and I would like to tender into evidence D26/5 and D27/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. No objection? They are admitted into evidence. I will turn now to Counsel Pavkovic to ask whether there is any Defence counsel prepared to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you. Mr. Luka Susak has some questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will try to be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Witness, you said the village guards had been established, and you also told us that there had been no commander of such village guards; but was there a person who was in charge of scheduling and assigning people to village guards?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We organised ourselves on our own, and sometimes we would say, "Well, today I'm in charge of assigning people." But it was almost like a joke; we didn't have a real command at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about command; I would just like to know whether anyone was in charge of recording who went where.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: We did not have any kind of register like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know Slavko Milicevic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he a member of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Counsel Susak. We may start with the cross-examination of -- Mr. Blaxill, would you prefer to take a break now, and then we start in 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands, but if you care to take the break now, I would be quite content with that, and we can get started afresh then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, all right. So we will take a 30-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 10.55 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I think it might be appropriate at this point if I refer Your Honours to the book from which extracts were used in the last hearing, and you required that we should have this book in its entirety ready for service. It has been served this morning on all Defence counsel. Copies have been made available and ready for the use of yourselves, Your Honours, and the only thing is we don't have a number for it yet. So perhaps if a number could be assigned, that will assist us in future cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I wonder, then, if that exhibit, please, could be shown to the witness. But at page 99, 15 lines up from the bottom, that is the only reference I shall be making to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, good morning to you, sir. My name is Michael Blaxill. I am one of the prosecutors assigned to this case. I do have a few questions to ask as a result of your evidence this morning, but the first thing I will ask you is: Have you served any time served in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If you look at an entry 15 lines from the bottom of that page numbered 99, does that reference in fact refer to yourself?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And is that your signature to the right-hand side in the last-but-one column?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, I would ask you, if you would, to indicate why it is at that particular time you served from the 8th of April, 1992, until October the 1st of 1992, and that appears to be the end of your official HVO service. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't spend this whole period in the HVO. I didn't join the HVO in April as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, the entry for the 8th of April, you have signed for the details in that form. It does say the 8th of April of that year is your start date and the 1st of October is your finish date. Are you saying that those dates are not accurate?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying that the dates are not accurate, but simply I know that I wasn't in the army in that period. For instance, in April, I wasn't in the army. But it's written here as if I had been. I don't know how to put it. This is a written document, maybe for the benefit of shares or for some other reason this date is indicated. I don't know why this date has been written down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So were you in fact, though, a serving HVO member, let us say, at the date of the 30th of September, 1992? In other words, the day before you appear to have had your service finished, according to the book. Were you actually in the HVO then?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: But which year?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, not officially, as a professional soldier. I was still not a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Does that mean you were some form of reserve soldier?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the reserve, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Again, though, it does seem perhaps a little strange that at October '92, things being as they were, that you appear then to have ceased service. Is that so, or in fact is that date wrong?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, my service didn't cease then. I started officially in May or June in 1993. I don't know exactly when I joined as a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So you can't really explain why those particular two dates have been applied to you in that form, in that document?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: This period until April, I think that is why, because until April 1992, I was still working in my enterprise, my company. And then they told us simply not to come to work any more, and so I stopped working. Perhaps they wanted to link up this period so that there would be no interruption in my years of service; maybe that is why they linked up these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did anybody explain that to you when you, in fact, signed alongside this information, when you placed your signature there?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Only now do I see that one really has to read carefully something that you sign. They didn't explain it well to us at all. They said that they would be linking our work service with our military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. So you say that during 1992 you were serving in the village guard. That is right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And for a portion of the year that was a joint guard with Muslim neighbours?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was joint guard with the Muslims until the 19th of October, '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You've indicated that the weapons you were supplied with came from the local TO, is that correct, the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They gave the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you not have anybody who at least acted as a kind of coordinator or person to help run the village guard and issue instructions to the various groups who were patrolling?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: There was no coordination at all. We organised ourselves and we assigned the shifts. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Since the shelling started, because we were told that we had to self-organise ourselves, and this was announced over the public media. They simply announced that because of the danger of sabotage groups and air raids, to save the women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Therefore, performing those guard duties who did you believe that you were guarding the civilians from? Who was the enemy at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would it be true to say that, in fact, that then became essentially the forces of the Serbs, the Bosnian Serb forces? Would than right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Bosnian Serbs together with the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So as far as you were concerned as a member of the village guard, that was the focus of your attention, it was the -- what has been described as the Serb aggression. There were no problems with your Muslim neighbours at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have any problems with our Muslim neighbours, and that is why we kept guard duty together. As we didn't have sufficient number of weapons, we would pass on the weapons on to our neighbours. For example, I gave my gun to my neighbour Fakan because he didn't have one at the time, or at least he pretended he didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So when you were performing that guard duty did you have at least any contact with any other units of guards, or did you have contact with any form of headquarters place to report anything that might happen?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Most frequently we were divided into small groups, and it was easiest to organise the shifts and for us to co-operate amongst ourselves, because we had our own tasks. In the event of an air raid, we would want families to go to the shelters because we feared air raids most.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you have any form of communications, however, in case your community was attacked, that you could summon some help or you could report what was happening? Did you have any lines of communication for that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: There were telephone lines, but we could, for instance, call the civilian police if we needed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Nenad Santic at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Nenad Santic became a member of the HVO and was very much involved in the organisation of HVO and indeed of the village guards in the overall area of Ahmici, particularly Santici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Were you aware of any role performed by Mr. Nenad Santic in organising or controlling village guards and/or HVO personnel in and around Santici-Ahmici area?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Nenad Santic, in another area, in the area of Zume, for instance, this is another part that is divided by a kind of veil, and so we didn't have much contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, if I may move on then to the date the 19th of October of 1992. You made mention of being on guard and that you saw some people moving by a fence. Can you be a bit more explicit as to what you mean by people moving by a fence and where was the fence?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a fence, it was a hedge, like a hedge. It was in parts quite high and in other parts it was low, and they passed north of that hedge, 10, 15 metres behind the hedge towards the west, and they passed along that path. There was a large group of uniformed men. It was just before dark fell, so we couldn't see them well, but one did wonder what so many soldiers were doing there at that time. When I said -- I said to Fahran, "Why won't you keep watch duty with us?" After that we couldn't see the soldiers any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that you cannot say whether those soldiers were, in fact, HVO personnel, or whether they were ABiH personnel or a group of village guards wearing combat kit? I mean, you cannot tell the difference?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I can tell the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You said it was very dark -- it was getting dark and that you couldn't really tell who they were.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I could tell, because we were together with the Muslims keeping village guards, and this was not customary movement, because this is a field owned by Muslims and it was never used to go around houses, because if you went up to a house you would use the main road. So we were already suspicious at seeing them crossing the fields rather than taking paths.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But I put it again to you, Mr. Papic, that you are not able for certainty to say whether they were troops from the ABiH or whether they were from the HVO. You couldn't make it out clearly enough. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: But we could intimate. We could assume that they were Muslims, that they were Muslim troops, because it was not customary. But we were not disturbed by that so much that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Indeed. You said you had no reason to suspect problems with the Muslims at that time, and I'm suggesting that what you're saying now is just speculating after the event and suggesting that these people were necessarily Muslim soldiers. Mr. Papic, the following morning, the 20th of October of 1992, you say there was firing very early on, so you endeavoured to get your family away from your home and you did so and went into the woods, I believe to the south of your property. Is that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Southeast from my house we headed to the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you were in the woods you -- did you send your family on to seek shelter elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did send my family away to seek shelter, because that was the only direction they could go along to safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe that was the direction, was it, of Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe you said, sir, also that your cousin Mr. Dragan Papic went in that same direction with his family -- or lady members of his family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Can you advise me, sir, why you, therefore, remained in the woods? Why didn't you go and seek shelter with your family, follow your cousin?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Because my house was exposed to direct gunfire, and I thought they would shoot again so I wanted to see what was happening. In the meantime, my mother and younger brother had stayed behind, and I wanted to go back to see what had happened to them. That was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Were there other male Croats in the woods with you at that time whose families had gone on and they were, just young men of military age in the woods?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was Goran Papic, Rafael Milicevic, Ivica Papic. I can't recall any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Were any of you armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Amongst us? I had a M-48 rifle, and I think there was another M-48 rifle but I don't know who had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I would advise you we've heard in this very Chamber from Mr. Mehmed Ahmic. You know him, you've mentioned him. He referred to a number of people he saw in the woods who were using weapons, and there were a number of people he saw, and your name is amongst them; "Pero Papic, Slavko and Rafael Milicevic and a few other people. I didn't recognise the others. They were all my neighbours." So Mr. Ahmic was correct, sir, when he said that he would have seen you in the woods in company with some of these other people and indeed some of you armed. So he was correct in that description, would that be so?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I can immediately negate that because -- if he mentioned Slavko Milicevic. Slavko Milicevic wasn't in the house that day at all. He may have been guessing who was in the woods. Slavko Milicevic was in Split on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But he certainly refers to yourself and Rafael Milicevic and, of course, at that point early in the day Mr. Dragan Papic, all having been in the wood and you say that that is so. Now --

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan Papic was not in the wood at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, he had gone on through the woods to take his wife and family to shelter, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: He passed through the woods but very early on. Mehmed couldn't have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware of what Mr. Dragan Papic did for the rest of that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Until the end of that day I don't know at all what he did, I just know that he left, and then afterwards there were stories but I can't testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You are aware, are you, that your cousin, Mr. Dragan Papic, was a former JNA soldier doing his national service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Were you aware of any special skills he acquired during his JNA service like the ability to use a mortar?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, because we didn't discuss national service very much at all amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If I suggest to you, sir, something we've heard in this Chamber to the effect that Mr. Dragan Papic spent a good proportion of the day armed with a mortar in the region of Donja Rovna, would you -- would that come as a surprise to you, or is that something you have subsequently heard took place?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I heard that three or four days later, but people keep making things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Sir, you say that later on, after this initial firing that occurred on the 20th of October, there was a call upon Croats to surrender, and then was there some more firing after that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: After the conflict do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: After the call you say came from the minaret, did you hear -- was there any more shooting? Did anything more happen?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there was more shooting but it was not for very long. It was of lesser intensity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Eventually that shooting came to an end. And had you remained in the woods throughout the whole period?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, throughout that period. That was the only shelter we had, so our movement was limited to the woods. Even the HVO army that was passing fired directly at us into the woods. We were afraid. We didn't know it was them. We thought it was the Muslims that were about to surround us. They were coming from the eastern side. The fire from coming from the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So in point of fact, you're saying that you even came under fire from some HVO people at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So we've heard description that the cause of the conflict on the 20th of October was essentially a road checkpoint set up by Muslim forces near the cemetery, and that passed -- an HVO force trying to get to Jajce to fight in the lines was stopped. Does that description agree with your memory of what you were told?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: That is what I learned subsequently. I learned that later. Maybe it was the 22nd when I learned why the conflict had erupted. At first I thought that the only -- their only goal was to attack us, our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But the reality of it is that the violence that occurred was when the HVO attacked that roadblock to try and get it removed, and that's what the outbreak of violence between the two forces was all about, isn't at that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. I think not, because the first shots, I think, were fired at my house, according to what I learned later on in the next few days. The first shots were fired at my house, a burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You were unable, I presume, sir, to see who fired those shots?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see because there was a thick fog.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So we have foggy conditions. We have clearly what ended up in a forcible attack by the HVO to remove the roadblock, and, therefore, we can't be sure where those shots came from that first you say hit your premises?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? It wasn't an HVO attack, it was an attack by the Muslims forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yet prior to the outbreak of shooting, if I understand you correctly, the only thing that showed the presence of Muslim forces was the fact that they had set up a checkpoint, which is a different thing, wouldn't you agree, not an attack?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: May I stand up and show you the difference on the map in terms of area, so that I can show you the distance between the two? (Indicating) This is the hedge here, you see, and there were large groups of Muslim forces here, and the roadblock was here near the cemetery. There were trenches there, and there were also trenches in this part of the cemetery here, in the very corner. And here there's a large concrete fence, so they already had a man-made shelter. Later I learned they put up the barricades, and I went to see later on what had happened, because I was interested. I was curious. It's quite far. In my view, the aim was to attack these seven Croat houses because they wanted to eliminate us from there. They wanted to strategically link this part of territory and to cut across the bridge. We learned that later. They told us themselves that that was their goal, to link up with the Muslim parts of Gornja Rovna, Vranjska, and again Muslim settlements here. That was the closest way to link up their forces and territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I presume you were not serving in the military at the time, so with respect, isn't this just your subsequent speculation about what people must have --

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: It is my opinion, yes, my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, in the course of your evidence, you said that on that day, the 20th of October, Muslims were leaving the Ahmici area, is that correct, as well as Croats?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. The Muslims left the lower part, as far as I know. As for the upper part of Ahmici, I couldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You have said that they started to return to their homes when they were in fact called by Croat neighbours and invited to come back?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Croats invited them on the 21st, immediately, to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If the events in that day had been action by the ABiH, the Muslim forces, to secure territory or to clear out Croats, does that not seem inconsistent with the fact that Muslims then left the area, and it was the Croats who were inviting them back to their houses? That does seem an inconsistent pair of propositions.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, let me see; there is a contradiction. Their abortive attack caused them to retreat from that area, and troops came from outside that were meant to cause a dispute between good neighbours. This is what we learned later on. We were also surprised that heading that operation was Muris Ahmic, who was one of my closest neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what actually happened to Mr. Muris Ahmic? Is he still alive? Is he still around?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I know, because I learned later on what happened, and I know that he's not alive. But what actually happened to him, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When the Muslims started to return to that village, did you know anything about the terms in which they would do so, or any agreements reached between Muslims and Croats as to the sort of conditions that would prevail between them?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, all I know is what I heard on the media, rather on the radio. I know that the Croats invited them. I know that from media reports. As for any personal knowledge, I couldn't have any. I couldn't deal with whether people would come back or not. I had no decision-making powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe you've said, Mr. Papic, that you had some form of accident in -- was it February of 1993?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, in October, 1993, I had a car accident. The car I had at the time was a Zastava 750 -- sorry, not October; it was in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, if I may ask, sir, how badly injured were you in that car accident? I believe you did have to go to hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very serious accident. I spent four days in the hospital in Travnik. I had an arm fracture, I had an interior haemorrhage, and they told me that my heart was also injured, and I had to rest for about 20 days. I'm not an expert in medicine, but anyhow, I spent four days in hospital in Travnik. After that, I was transferred; due to the shelling that came from Vlasic Mount, I was transferred somewhere else because they didn't want to risk any further problems. So I was transferred to the hospital in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When were you able to return home after your hospital treatment?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I returned home on the 3rd of -- on the 3rd of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I presume, sir, did you stay home recuperating from your injuries for the weeks that followed that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I still had splints on my leg. I had a bandage on my arm which I had to carry for a while. I stayed at home for about ten days, and then my sister suggested that I should come to her house in Busovaca, because my wife was having a difficult time because I couldn't move. So she suggested that we came to her place in Busovaca. So we went there, and I don't know exactly when it happened, but it may have been around the 14th or the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Of March; is that correct? 14th or 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And so if we go one month later, to the 15th and 16th of April, I believe you did say that you were still in Busovaca at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: In fact, just for the record, if I could ask you: Can you tell me what the exact date of your car accident was, the date in February?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. On the 10th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Do you need the exact time of the accident?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If you recall the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: At 3 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. So obviously you had no personal experience of the events in Ahmici on the 16th of April, 1993? That would be correct to say?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have any personal experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You of course were a cousin of Mr. Dragan Papic and have described that he was a forester and from time to time would wear a uniform. Could you describe what types of uniform he would wear at different times?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Most frequently he would wear only one part of the uniform, the upper part of the uniform, and he would wear the normal trousers. He didn't have any special trousers, any special clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: What colour was the upper part uniform he would wear?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Greenish. Green and grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would that be described as a camouflage uniform, or is the camouflage a different type of pattern?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, you can describe it as a camouflage uniform, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Mr. Papic wearing or in possession of a black uniform, or part of uniform?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I only know that he had a blue vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
