utterances.text: Blue can be many things: Can you say how dark or how light that blue was?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Dark blue, yes. Dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Now, you've described Mr. Papic as one who did not come out with political comments or particularly nationalist comments. I think, to quote you, he only liked motor cars, not politics.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: However, as relations with the Muslims deteriorated in the early part of 1993, was there any change in attitude on the part of Mr. Dragan Papic, if only to be more protective towards Croats, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, of course, we all changed in that period. The population as a whole changed. People no longer trusted one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So, true to say that a political situation like that in fact you say produced a change in everybody; you couldn't avoid changing, perhaps. Yeah?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, everybody. It's very difficult not to change in such a period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I believe at the time it was customary that particularly on religious holidays or something like that that national flags would be flown on people's homes. If it was a Muslim holiday, the Muslims, and Croats, it would be on the Croat holiday. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Is it true, therefore, that the house of Ivo Papic, the flags would fly on the appropriate festive days, just like any other Croat family celebrating such an event?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, a Croat flag was flown.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Do you recall that at times when the tensions had grown greater between the communities, that the Croat flag in fact remained longer on the Papic household? It wasn't just up there for the odd religious holiday?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't pay much attention to that, because at the time, it was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: At the time you say it was normal to see Croat flags or any flags on houses quite a lot. Sir, Mr. Mehmed Ahmic, you stated he was not liked by people because he ran up a lot of debts. Is it true that people also perhaps disliked his political attitude? Did he assume a political attitude when he was in the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't think that that was the problem. And I think that Croats liked him more than the Muslims; that's my personal opinion. There were other reasons, of course, and I learned through conversations with people about him. And that was my impression at the time, the impression that I got from other people as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Papic did possess a rifle, did he not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You were aware of his occupation as a forester, I believe, sir? But you --

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Sorry, I spoke over you; I apologise.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he personally was issued with that rifle. I don't know if it belonged to him or whether it belonged to the forestry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Right. Perhaps I'll rephrase it to be more accurate: Were you aware that he had possession of a rifle?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did that rifle have a telescopic sight, for accuracy?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Was that a rifle that is a single-shot rifle of some accuracy?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I think it's a kind of rifle with a five-bullet clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But to your recollection, do you ever recall seeing Mr. Dragan Papic carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: When he would go to work or coming home from work, yes, I know that he would carry it at that time. But only occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Could you -- or do you recall, of the members of the Papic family living in the house of Ivo Papic, can you recall what motor cars they owned between them on or about the 15th of April, 1993? Do you know what cars they happened to own?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: At home, there were always quite a few vehicles around their house. According to my knowledge, Dragan had an orange Stojadin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: As you lived in the vicinity, had you ever noticed Mr. Dragan driving different cars? Possibly ones he's repairing for friends, I suppose, but have you seen him driving a variety of different cars over the years?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would see him driving different cars. This would last only for two or three hours; he would only test the vehicles. He would sometimes go to Vjetrenice in order to test the engine, to see if the engine would heat up. This is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'd like just a brief moment to confer with my colleagues, if you please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Papic, thank you, sir, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now call upon Counsel Pinter. Before I do so, I wonder whether at some stage we could hear from the Prosecutor or Defence counsel a few comments on this document, P353. I wonder whether they could shed some light on the purpose and contents of this document. Because now we have received a copy, but it's in Croatian. And probably either party can -- or both parties could explain what it is about, at some stage; not necessarily now. It's for you to decide. I mean, we would at some stage like to have some light on this. Probably the Prosecutor could first of all try to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that last week, during the Friday hearing, we disclosed as evidence -- and I don't have the exact number, but I hope it can be found easily -- we disclosed one page together with a translation of the first page and the title of the document. So I think that as regards the translation, this would be enough, because it's the same form. I think in this way you can orient yourself. But if you wish, we can give you some additional translation. But I believe that the translation of that page has already been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You're right. I was wrong. I think at that time that we did not have a translation for certain indications; we didn't know, for example, what "P" stood for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, you're right, but I cannot help you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: If the Defence counsel could perhaps tell us? They told us that it could mean reservist. But you're not sure? Thank you. Thank you very much. Ms. Pinter, you have the floor for the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, the Prosecutor has shown you a document -- a list take is now in front of you, and he wanted your explanation of the dates on it. And I have a question related to that. I want to know whether you were employed at the time during the period from April until October 1992. Did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I was not employed from the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: At that time, were you a member of the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor asked you about the village guard, he referred to them as some kind of duty, some kind of obligation. My question to you is whether it was compulsory for people to be members of the village guard, or was it simply on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The fact that we organised ourselves meant that it was not compulsory. Dragan usually avoided the village guard, because he was working most of the time. And people were self-organised, on the basis of houses and neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In response to a Prosecutor's question, you said that the local Territorial Defence provided you with weapons. I would like to know whether the village of Ahmici had their Territorial Defence, or whether it belonged to the Vitez unit.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Members of the Territorial Defence were both Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, but was it under the jurisdiction of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: We were discussing the objective of the village guards. You said it was as a protection against air raids?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the main purpose of the village guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us, could you tell us whether, apart from the air raids, there was any other form of danger that you were exposed to, were there any robberies at the time, any attacks?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we all knew that in view of the situation we had to perform guard duty because there were lots of sabotage units that could enter the village at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did that occur? Did you ever find any unknown persons in your area during your guard duty? If you can remember that.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can. I can answer your question. We did not have any authority to stop people to ask them questions. We were simply able to follow the situation, to observe the situation, and we could report to the people we knew, if there was anything suspicious going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination, did the name of Fahrudin Ahmic came up. Is he still alive?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I'm saying that because there are two persons with the same name, and he's your neighbour, he's still your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The night of the 19th, while you were performing guard duty, the night between the 19th and the 20th of October, you mentioned that there was a group of people near the hedge. In response to a Prosecutor's question, you said that in view of the location where these people were, you concluded that they were members of the BH army, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, because very -- it was very unusual for soldiers to move around that area, around the field. So that was something strange. I believed, and after we asked Fahrudin Ahmic about that, he probably told them to move away. So after that, we no longer see them. So we didn't expect that any conflict would occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So when you told Fahrudin Ahmic that you had seen a group of people on the field near the hedge, did he become frightened? Did he show any interest in knowing who it was?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was as if he already knew. And he did not provide us with any answer to our questions. He simply went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In response to a Prosecutor's question regarding the whereabouts of Dragan, you stated that he had been in Donja Rovna. At any point in time later on, not that day, but sometime later on, did you ever discuss his whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, partly. But it is in my nature not to want to know everything. Sometimes it's not good to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You met with Mr. Santic at a particular location, and you saw that Dragan met with Mr. Santic at a particular location; could you tell us how far that location is and could you also show the exact location of Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: They met in this area here. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And the house of Anto Papic is near the railway

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please switch on the other microphone, because the interpreters cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: The house of Anto Papic is here, Dragan and Nenad met in this area here. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How far is it from the house of Nenad Santic? How long does it take, half an hour, one hour to cover the distance?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, no. Only -- it's a ten-minute walk. There are shortcuts. Depends on which way you go. If you follow the road then it is much longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was that the usual way that you would -- the usual path that you would take?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Again in response to a Prosecutor's question, you said that -- that your house was hit by the HVO. Can you now say that it was only the HVO who opened fire on your house? Later on you stated that there was an attack on the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I deny that. I said that my house was not attacked by the HVO members but the BH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Is it your opinion or were you told by Muris what the purpose of the attack was, I mean, the attack of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. This is not my opinion. Muris Ahmic told me about the purpose of the attack, because he led the operation, and according to him the operation was supposed to be led by Sivro Bahtija who was already a member of the Territorial Defence at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: This means that when you spoke about the cause of the attack earlier on and when you were describing the events that took place on the 21st of October, you were telling -- you were saying what Muris Ahmic had told you, not your opinion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is what Muris Ahmic told us. That's how we learned about the purpose of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: After the attack on the 21st of October, 1992, did Croats go to Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: After the attack, that is after the 21st of October, on the 22nd and on the 23rd we no longer dared to go to Ahmici, because we were told that we would be beaten up if they see us in Ahmici. We didn't need to go to the Upper Ahmici because the village guards were in the lower area. They threatened us, so we simply didn't dare go there. They told Andjelko Vidovic, for example, that they no longer wanted to see us in the upper part of the village of Ahmici. I can show you on the map, for example. To this area we could move freely, but after this we were not allowed. (Indicating) Later on we saw them digging a trench, but they told us that it was not a trench. They told us that it was a well, but we realised that a trench had been dug up over there and that's why they didn't want us to pass there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In February 1993, you had your accident and you stated the date and the time of the accident. You have the relevant documentation?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Where were you hospitalised, intensive care or traumatology department?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the intensive care ward but everything was all mixed up in the Travnik hospital at the area -- at that time, because it was in a kind of a shelter because of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Dragan Papic wore a camouflage uniform, you said. I wanted to know whether he also wore a forestry uniform.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, when he -- he would change into another uniform. He wouldn't wear the camouflage uniform all the time, and it was only natural that he also wore a forestry uniform because he would go to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were Muslim flags also flown on the houses?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, during religious holidays or on other such occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How long do their holidays last, religious holidays, do you know?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't really know how long they last.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Finally, let me ask you to repeat why the locals did not like Mehmed Ahmic. Maybe the Prosecutor missed this point, so could you tell us what the reasons were? Was it his political views or were there other reasons? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Mehmed did all kinds of things. He engaged in business. He would burglarise his own shop to collect some insurance money, and we all knew that. Even he didn't conceal the fact. Then he would owe a lot of people in the village money. I also did some things for him but I can't say that he owed me money, he didn't, but many complained about that. They complained about his behaviour, and he was accepted in the leadership of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: No, but we're talking about the local people.

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In front of Ivo Papic's house, until the war -- or, rather, until you were there, that is until February 1993, were there cars in front of that house?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were they cars owned by the Papic family?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: No. There were other cars that were being repaired there. They would stay there for two, three, four days.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. One more question. After the 20th of October when you saw Dragan, did Dragan tell you where he was on the 20th of October?

utterances.speaker: PERO PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said he was in Donja Rovna, but I didn't ask him about any further details, nor was I interested in the details as to his movements there. In any event, he spent the whole day there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. There will be no objection, I assume, to the witness being released. Mr. Papic, thank you so much for testifying in court. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we move on to our next witness, I would like to draw your attention to a motion which had been filed some time ago, the 11th of February. It has been told to me by the Registrar that we have not yet taken any action on the granting of safe conduct for the witness Josip Vidovic. It was probably a mistake. I was pretty sure that we had already issued an order on the issue of safe conduct. We will do so right away, but before we proceed to the request of safe conduct, I would like to ask the Prosecutors whether they have any objection to such safe conduct. It's Mr. Josip Vidovic living in Santici, and the request was filed by the Defence Counsel Susak on the 11th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: There is no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will issue this, and I apologise for this mistake or -- I don't know how to say. Shall we bring in the next witness, Mr. Goran Males?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Goran Males. I would like to ask you to make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may be seated. I will call upon counsel Pinter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Males.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Would you please introduce yourself?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: My name is Goran Males. I was born on the 24th of January, 1967 in Busovaca municipality in Podjele.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I'm a soldier, a member of the Special Units. I'm a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Since when have you been living in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I have been living in Vitez since 1967.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Before you settled in Vitez, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I lived at Rijeka in Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance could this aerial photograph be removed so that we can see better the bigger picture in the background on the board? Mr. Males, can you speak up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Will you please take the pointer on your right, you can extend it if necessary, and could you please point to Rijeka, where you lived before you went to Vitez, then where Podjele is. You can take off the headphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Rijeka, it's this area. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Find Vitez first, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Just a moment. This is Vitez municipality, all of this. Rijeka is here. In fact, it extends as far as this point. Then comes Donja Rovna in continuation. This also is Rijeka, up to here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Will you please show us where Podjele is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Podjele. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. You may take your seat.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who were the majority population in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The Croats were the majority population.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were there some Muslim -- in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, there were some.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What were the relationships like between Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How far is Rijeka from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It is about three and a half to four kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about the first conflicts in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: As far as my personal knowledge is concerned, I don't have any personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any knowledge as to where the first conflict between the Muslims and the Croats broke out?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: In Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where you were on the 19th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I was in Podjele, Busovaca municipality, after seeing off the relatives of my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you recall that day so well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Where were your mother's relatives going?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: My mother's relatives were leaving to the territory under Serb army control.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Simply they couldn't organise their lives to stay on in the vicinity. There was the village of Merdani and the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What ethnicity is your mother?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: My mother is of Serbian nationality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So there were Serbs living in Podjele, or were they the minority?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The majority population was Serbs. There were some Croats and one Muslim family.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So your mother's family, on the 19th of October, was leaving Podjele?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are any members of your family living in Podjele today?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, no one is living there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. Will you please describe now your return journey from Podjele to Rijeka, but before that will you please tell us whether you had any property, or a house or some woods there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, we did have some property. We had a house and some land, and that is why I spent a lot of time there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So it means that formerly you were living in Vitez but you spent a lot of time in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm being told that it is time for our break. We were anyway going on to another area now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Excellent. We'll take a break, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pinter?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Mr. Males, we stopped when you were at Podjele to see off your mother's family, who had moved out.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Podjele to see off my mother's relatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you speak up a little?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Podjele; I was seeing off my mother's family.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: After that, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Which road did you take?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The main road going from Kaonik to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you go by car, did you use public transport, or on foot, by bike? How did you go?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I went on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: For one reason: To hitchhike, to stop a vehicle along the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You didn't have a car at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The road you took, taking you to Rijeka, does it pass through Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When I finish my question, wait a moment and then answer it, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to take the pointer and point on the map the road you took from Podjele to Rijeka. Please turn towards the microphone so we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: (Indicating) this is Podjele, and I started from Podjele, following this road. I reached Kaonik; from Kaonik, I went along the main road towards Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you meet anyone along the way?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: At Nadioci, I met some Croats, men of Croatian nationality, who warned me not to go toward Ahmici, but to take another path via Rasko Polje, Radak's bridge, and Rijeka. I didn't follow their advice, and I went on along the main road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Before you went on, and when they were warning you -- you can sit down. Did they tell you, when they warned you not to continue along that road, what was happening in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. They said that something was happening to the effect that the road was blocked.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Why didn't you listen to their advice?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Because across Rasko Polje and Radak's bridge, it was not pleasant to take that road at the time. It was night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were you an active-duty soldier at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: An active-duty soldier?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you have a uniform and weapon that evening?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. I was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When you went on from Nadioci towards Ahmici, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: At the Sangaj restaurant, I was stopped again by Croats who told me that something was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was it a barricade, or ... ?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I don't know. Again, I didn't listen to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "up there"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I mean near the cemetery. In a hollow. The cemetery was on the left-hand side, and there was an uphill slope on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Again, I didn't do as I was told, so I went on. And when I got to some 10 or 15 metres away from the cemetery, they said "Stop."

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The Bosnia and Herzegovina army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How could you tell it was the BH army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Because I had already been warned that they were preparing something there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. I just saw shadows. When I walked up to them, I saw that they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How could you tell they were soldiers, and that they belonged to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: As I approached them, they immediately asked my ID particulars: My name, my date of birth, my surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I told them my particulars, and they said "Wait a minute."

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How many men gathered round you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Roughly 100.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were they standing in the middle of the road, or on the side?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Some were standing on the road; others were jumping across a fence, coming from the cemetery, actually from the cemetery itself. And from this uphill slope, they were coming down this little hill into the hollow where the road passed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were near the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. Right facing the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you describe to the Court what these men who surrounded you looked like? Were they wearing civilian clothes, or uniforms? Were they armed? Was it a group of men, or were they organised? Could you describe that for us.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It was an organised group of men. Most of them were wearing camouflage uniforms. They were armed. There were some civilians. Very few, but they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How could you tell that they were BH army members?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It was my assessment that the Croats would not have held me there, because they asked for my particulars as to when I was born, where I was coming from, where I was going, who I was, what I was, who my parents were, my brothers, my sisters; they wanted to know all those particulars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you remember today what they said to you --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: -- what they wanted from you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: They insulted me. They didn't ask for anything else, just my particulars. They asked whether I had come across anyone else on my way.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did they threaten you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I heard somebody from the group saying "let's kill him and throw him into the channel. Let's gouge his eyes out." And things like that, all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you feel that you were in danger?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How did this whole incident end? Did anyone react, did you recognise anyone, did someone come up? What happened?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: A person came out of the group and said he was going to get the commander. I waited. They came back, some of them, but they just kept asking me more questions. They pointed a lamp at me, 10 centimetres away from my eyes. They wrote down some more details: My date of birth, where I was born, where I was coming from, where I was going. They left, apparently to fetch the commander again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did the commander come?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The second time they came, nobody asked me anything. The third time they went to fetch the commander, and then he came, this commander of theirs, who asked me my first and last names. When I told them my first and last names, he said, "Let him go. Let him pass." By his voice, I am of the opinion that it was Fikret Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you knew Fikret Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Since primary school. Because we went to the primary school at Donja Dubravica, at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you know why the roadblock had been put up at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you know at the time the reason for putting up the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, I did not know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you personally see the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The roadblock was in the direction of the chapel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you see what it consisted of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, it consisted of a village fence that we called Baskija.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: That fence, was it an obstacle, or could it have been used as an obstacle for vehicles?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, it could. It could be an obstacle for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you learn subsequently why the roadblock had been put up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The road was blocked so as to prevent the people of Busovaca from going to Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: At the time were you an active duty soldier or were you a reservist?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I was in the reserves.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When did you become an active duty soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In '90 what?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: We would see each other in front of the Sumarija, the forestry company when my neighbour was purchasing fuel wood, and I would also see him in Vitez in cafes known as Fistas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What kind of relationship did you have with him? Were you friends or acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: We were just acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you remember today what Dragan Papic looked like in those days when you would come across him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Dragan had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What kind of a beard?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It was quite big.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you look at him today? Was his beard like that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, his beard was bigger than that and thicker. He wasn't shaved on the sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When you spoke to Dragan in the cafes, when you came across him, as you've said, did you spend enough time with him to be able to say that in your conversations Dragan manifested any kind of nationalist feelings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. In our conversations this did not appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What did you discuss then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Mostly girls.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you discuss politics at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was he interested in politics? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I wouldn't think he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of what he liked to do apart from his regular work, if you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: That would be all, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you very much Counsel Pinter. Counsel Pavkovic, any cross-examination by other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, no other Defence counsel wishes to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, my name is Franck Terrier. I am one of the Prosecution attorneys, and I'm going to ask a few questions after the testimony that you have just given. First of all, you told us a few moments ago that you are today a professional soldier and that you belong to a special unit. Can you be more specific about that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. I joined the professional army for one reason. It was the best paid army in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On what date did you join that army as a professional?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: On the 21st of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What does a "special unit" mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: A "special unit" means that we have to be ready to carry out any tasks assigned to us in peacetime and in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Does that also mean that you had special training?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What is your rank?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I have no rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So that means you're just a soldier, a private?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where was your unit stationed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Now it is stationed in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry. Counsel Pinter?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are questions regarding the current occupation of the witness, and I would rather that he not be questioned about his present occupation as that is not covered by the indictment. The witness has told us where he works and since when, but what he's now doing I don't think is important or relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The witness told us that he was a soldier belonging to a special unit. It goes without saying that -- that I can obtain from this witness that I wish to cross-examine and whose credibility concerns me, I wish to have some precision as to what those special units are and what are the current activities of a professional unit, but I will cover that very quickly and go back to the period of 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Terrier, because we have just learned from the witness that he joined that special unit on the 21st of August, 1995, so that Attorney Pinter is right. Nevertheless, we too would like to know what the tasks are of those special units. Just a few words about it. Then I would be grateful if you would go back to the period of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, could you then specify for us, in the case of a conflict or case of difficulty, the special tasks of the unit that you belong to today?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: You know yourself, the defence of the State. In peacetime we assist people when building roads. That is the engineers, but we as the infantry have no duties. We just secure military buildings and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I think that we will have to be satisfied with that answer, Mr. President. I'm going now back to the period of '92-'93. A moment ago, witness, in answer to questions by the Defence lawyer, you said that you were first a reservist in the HVO and then an active duty soldier. Could you specify the dates when you became an HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: A soldier in the HVO? Could you please clear -- make that question clearer? When I became a soldier or when I was in the reserve?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm asking you both. When did you become a reservist and when you became an active duty soldier.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I became an active duty soldier at the beginning of the conflict, and before that for a very short period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, witness, to finish your answer which doesn't appear to be complete? Can you specify the dates if you know them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I am afraid I do not know the dates just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in that case -- at least give us a more precise indication of the period during which you became an active duty soldier of the HVO? Surely you can remember the period.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The summer of '92. I was a reservist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps you're not understanding me. My question is: In what period did you become an active duty soldier of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I became an active duty soldier of the HVO on the 16th of March, 1993 when the conflict actually broke out in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said the 16th of March, 1993? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As from the 16th of March, 1993 you were an active duty soldier of the HVO. Where were you on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993 I was in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Which unit of the HVO did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pinter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the examination-in-chief the witness was asked a question about the year of 1992 and the 20th of October, 1992. In his testimony, we did not discuss his affiliation with any military in the year of 1993, nor was any mention made of the events that took place in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, but the Prosecutor has the right to ask questions concerning the relevant times, that is the year of 1993. Why not? You are familiar with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. There is a Rule, according to which the witness can be asked questions which go outside the strict framework of the examination-in-chief. That is the main -- the direct-examination. It seems to me that the question that is asked by Mr. Terrier is a relevant question because it goes to the relevant events. Therefore, we will allow the Prosecutor to continue with the questions relating to the period of March and April in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us to which unit of the HVO you belonged on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I belonged -- just a second -- to the Novi Travnik unit which was called Kralj Tomislav unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it not a brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? You were a soldier at the time. Could you specify the unit to which you belonged in terms of battalion, company and so on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I was a member of a company which was under the jurisdiction of Vitez municipality. Vitez municipality had a company of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who was the commander who issued orders to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, the commander of the company.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The commander of my company, to tell you the truth, is still unknown to me. I still don't know who the commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of any officer or non-commissioned officer under whose orders you were during that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. It was Mr. Karlo Grabovac who was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What were his duties?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened on the 16th of April, 1993? Could you briefly describe the events of that day, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It was the second conflict that broke out on the territory of the Vitez municipality. I was asleep at the time, and my mother woke me up and she wanted to know what was happening. She said, "Dear child, what is going on?" There was shooting, and I went out of the house and I realised that the situation was terrible, so I went to Rijeka, to the farm, to our property, to see what was happening with my property. I didn't want anyone to destroy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: So I got there, I got to the farm, and realised that everything was okay. However, there was shooting going on all over the place, and I went to the area called Cerveno Burce and I remained up there throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you say that you remained on that hill in the area of Cerveno Burce --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It's B-r-d-c-e.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said that you stayed there throughout the conflict. Could you be more specific? How long did you stay there? Could you give us any dates?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Well, I stayed there for one year, approximately. The duration of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please be more specific. At that time, you were an active-duty soldier; why did you stay there for one year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Well, we were defending our parts; that is, the area of the village of Vranjska. We were defending our houses, the houses that were behind the lines, and at that time they were only 30 or 40 metres away from the front line. What were we supposed to do? To let them occupy the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, but you received certain orders to stay there.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive any orders. I simply went to the front line in order to defend my property, in order to save the lives of my family, of my parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong: You say that you were an active-duty soldier, that you belonged to a brigade, to a company, that you were a member of a military organisation and you were part of a certain military hierarchy, you had a commander, and on the 16th of April, you stayed in the vicinity of your property in order to protect it, and that you remained there for a period of one year. Throughout that year, you no longer had any contact with your military command, and you sort of remained outside the military milieu? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Throughout the war, we didn't pay much attention to the command. We didn't really know who the commander was. The idea was simply to protect our homes. There was no proper structure, proper organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would like to understand you, and I know that the HVO had certain problems in terms of structure and organisation at the time. However, I would like you to confirm the fact that during that particular year, while you were an active-duty soldier, you remained without any orders. It was a period of a conflict, and you did not receive any orders; you were involved in some kind of personal matter.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: During the war, no one was under any command on that line. There were very few of us, and the idea was to remain there, in that particular area. The command was not properly structured. There was no proper military set-up at that time, and I'm referring to the HVO. So one can say that it was a self-organised defence of our own village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm really trying hard to understand. Were you armed during that time, during that year while you were protecting your village?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: You mean the front line, when you say "property"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the front line.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. We had very little weaponry, and it would change hands on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can I have the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to show you the Document 353, page 35. Page 55. It's page 55, and not 35. Witness, could you please have a look at the line 21 from the top, on page 1.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you find it? Could you please follow that line, and tell me whether the signature that figures at the end of the line is your signature.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the period that is indicated here on the document is the period during which you were a member of the HVO in 1992, and then up to 1995. Is that the correct period?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. The information is not correct, because this was done for the purpose of distribution of shares.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific, and tell us something more about this distribution of shares. Are you speaking about some kind of compensation for the services provided to the HVO in the form of shares?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes. Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is that the reason -- and please correct me if I'm wrong -- that we count the number -- that you count the number of months of service within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. But the date is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So why did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: This document has been signed, but you can see yourself that something was typed over this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, I could be more specific. This was done on two separate occasions, and in relation to the same number. There is a text here that was typed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I didn't at first understand what you meant. Could you tell us what the letter "P" stands for? It is on the right-hand side of the page, in the fourth column.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Column number 4, on the right side?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Actually it's in the middle of the page. On the line that refers to you, there is a column, and there is a letter "P "in it, at the same level.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I found it. I don't know. I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, were you compensated for the services provided to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: After the war, we were given shares, but these shares are not active yet. And I hope something will come out of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This type of compensation, did it involve -- was it applied only to active-duty soldiers, or to reservists as well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It was distributed to everyone who was at the time in the war, and it concerned both Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, my question was perhaps more specific: The persons who were reservists at the time, did they have the right, however, to a certain compensation, namely the compensation -- the kind of compensation that you have just described?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: All members who during the war were defending their area are entitled to these shares, to be compensated in the form of shares.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, but from what you have just told us, is it not true that there isn't much difference between a reservist and an active-duty soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No. There isn't much difference when it comes to shares, because we were simply defending our parts. There were elderly people among us, women who prepared food at the front line, people who brought food. All these individuals are entitled to this type of compensation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, does this not mean that all members of the Croatian Community, all those who are of military age and can perform military service, are actually members of the HVO; and is it not true that the notion of reservist, the way we understand it in the context of other armies in Europe, was actually non-existent? Is it not true that there were no reservists at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, it is not true. We didn't have reservists because there were very few of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind these conditions, in October 1992, on the road between Kaonik and Ahmici, you learned that a roadblock had been set up in Ahmici, and you decided not to take the byroad to Vitez; you decided to go along that road. But you at that time had military duties, you had military duties within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: I took the main road for one reason: Several days before that, there was very heavy rainfall. It's a dirt road; it's not a tarmac road. And during the first conflict, I was a reservist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would really like to understand correctly what you're saying. You were about to go in the direction of the roadblock, and you decided to do that because there was no other way for you to get to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: No, I could take the road that goes along Rasko Polje and the Radak bridge; but because of very heavy rainfall several days prior to that, because of the muddy roads, I decided to take the Ahmici road. I was a civilian. At that moment, I wasn't carrying any weapons, and I thought that there was not any special reason why that roadblock had been set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But in spite of that, on two occasions, you were told not to continue in that direction but to take up some other road; this is what you told us.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But I didn't want to get dirty, and I was hoping that a vehicle would pass by and that someone would give me a lift to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who was the HVO soldier whom you encountered and told who you not to continue in that direction? Where was he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: He was not an HVO soldier. These people were villagers of Croatian nationality, and this happened in the area of the village of Nadioci and also near the cafe called Sangaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If we can have the assistance of the usher, please. Can the witness be shown the area photograph of Ahmici so he can show us the exact location of the Sangaj cafe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Terrier, do you have many questions left? You don't think you will finish the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I don't have many questions left, maybe 10 or 15 minutes, but I presume we have other obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, on this aerial photograph can we see the location of the Sangaj cafe?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: The Sangaj restaurant is just below the cemetery. You can see the parking-lot near the cemetery. Can I use the pointer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Please do, yes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: This is the parking area of the Sangaj restaurant. It's right here. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It's not the same facility as the one commonly referred to as "Bungalow"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This facility that you have just shown on the map, is it the same facility or a different facility as the one called "Bungalow"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: It's not the same place. The Sangaj cafe is here and the Bungalow is further down the road. I can show you the location of the Bungalow as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Terrier. We will adjourn and we will come back tomorrow at 9.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: at 1.33 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of February, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
